title: CS Intake: 'Bucketizer' Playbook & Quick-Frame Scoper for Enterprise Requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a lightweight, repeatable playbook that lets Sales/CS quickly aggregate similar enterprise feature asks, assign them to buckets, and produce a 10-minute 'Quick-Frame' scoping note for PM/Eng handoff. The goal is to reduce noisy one-off asks, accelerate first-pass scoping, and identify high-leverage requests for discovery. This ticket builds the process, templates, and a minimal dashboard for tracking arrival rate and bundle size.
acceptance_criteria: A repeatable 'Bucketizer' worksheet (spreadsheet + single-click filters) that CS can use in <15 minutes per batch
A one-page Quick-Frame template capturing problem statement, affected customers, expected business impact, rough implementation complexity (Low/Med/High), and a suggested next step
At least two Sales reps and two CS reps can run the flow end-to-end in a dry-run and produce output that PMs find actionable
A small dashboard (runbook + Looker/Sheets view) shows incoming requests, bucket labels, and estimated aggregate ARR opportunity per bucket
Documented handoff contract that includes required artifacts and a 72-hour PM response SLA for urgent buckets
success_metrics: Time-to-first-scope reduced from avg 6 business days to <48 business hours for prioritized buckets
% of incoming enterprise asks that are consolidated into a bucket increases to >=45%
PMs report >75% of Quick-Frame notes are actionable without follow-up clarifying calls
CS adoption: at least 3 deals/week processed through the playbook within 30 days of launch
approach_summary: Run a two-week pilot with a small CS pod. Phase 1: design Bucketizer schema and Quick-Frame template; Phase 2: pilot the worksheet and collect feedback; Phase 3: build lightweight dashboard and iterate on thresholds. Emphasize low-friction tooling (Sheets + Zapier or lightweight form) over heavy infra for initial rollout.
stakeholders: Eng: Lina Chen (runtime), Omar Diaz (console) - review feasibility
decisions: Use a simple spreadsheet-based 'Bucketizer' as the canonical first-pass aggregation tool to minimize friction
Quick-Frame should be strictly time-boxed to 10 minutes and no more than 1 page
Pilot will accept only non-bug feature asks with clearly stated customer names to avoid noise
Do not build an automated classifier in phase 1 — capture labeled examples for potential ML in phase 2
